html:
Smederevo Fortress is a huge medieval fortress on the Danube in eastern Serbia, built from 1428 to 1430 by Despot Đurađ Branković as the new capital of Serbia after Belgrade was handed to Hungary.

Its walls, with 25 towers, enclose a triangle of about ten hectares, one of the largest lowland fortresses in Europe. Serbia by then was a despotate squeezed between Hungary and the Ottomans, paying tribute to the sultan. The Ottomans took the fortress in 1439, lost it and took it for good in 1459, after which Serbia ceased to exist as a state for almost 350 years, until the uprisings of the 1800s. It was badly damaged by an ammunition explosion in 1941.
sum: Smederevo Fortress is a huge medieval fortress on the Danube in eastern Serbia, built from 1428 to 1430 by Despot Đurađ Branković as the new capital of Serbia after Belgrade was handed to Hungary.
